summary_paragraph: A woman with end-stage renal disease, type 2 diabetes, and a history of anticoagulation for thrombosis was admitted for abdominal pain and found to have cardiac tamponade due to a large pericardial effusion. Her condition was attributed to a supratherapeutic INR of 18.2 from warfarin, likely exacerbated by recent antibiotic use and liver dysfunction. She underwent urgent pericardiocentesis, draining 700 cc of bloody fluid, and received reversal agents including vitamin K, FFP, and factor IX. Her INR stabilized to 2.3 by discharge. Elevated liver enzymes and an enlarged gallbladder led to a diagnosis of chronic cholecystitis; simvastatin was discontinued. She developed transient right leg pain, but imaging showed no hematoma. Her BIPAP was adjusted after an episode of desaturation. She remained on dialysis and insulin therapy without complications and was discharged to extended care with a low sodium diet, medication changes, and close outpatient follow-up for INR monitoring and liver evaluation.
